headline_rows.evidence: FP WikiText PPL 13.901475; naive PTQ PPL 3,813,121.803327; FP ten-task mean 0.644169; PTQ mean 0.348671
headline_rows.impact: The universal one-click arbitrary FP/BF16-to-ternary retrofit claim is not supported.
headline_rows.limitation: Dense Qwen2.5-1.5B tested setup; not a theorem for every architecture.

headline_rows.evidence: best row-scale QAT mean 0.499459; recovery vs PTQ +0.150788; gap vs FP -0.144710
headline_rows.impact: Training under ternary constraints recovers real signal, but not FP quality.
headline_rows.limitation: Row-scale QAT is a retrofit variant, not standard BitDistill.

headline_rows.impact: Paper-level BitDistill quality is not reproduced yet; the curve is still improving.
headline_rows.limitation: The 327.68M row improves over 163.84M but remains below the FP16 recovery gate.

headline_rows.impact: The attention-KD coefficient cannot be interpreted without matching loss reductions.
headline_rows.limitation: This is a local normalization diagnostic, not a claim that the paper coefficient is wrong.

headline_rows.evidence: one-scale TL2 RMS error 1.904230; exact row-scale RMS error 0.000197
headline_rows.impact: Row scales are model semantics, not optional metadata.
headline_rows.limitation: This supports I2_SR/row-scale contracts; TL2 row-scale support is not implemented.

headline_rows.evidence: I2_SR file 1211.3 MiB, PPL 38.8477, prompt 211.67 tok/s, decode 19.07 tok/s; Q4_K_M file 940.4 MiB, PPL 12.8112
headline_rows.impact: Dense row-scale ternary CPU execution works; audited Q4 comparison has 1.191x decode and 2.299x prefill speedups for I2_SR.
headline_rows.limitation: I2_SR is a speed-oriented proof of row-scale ternary runtime semantics. It improves decode speed versus FP16 and is faster than Q4_K_M in the audited run, but it is larger than Q4_K_M and has much worse PPL. It should not be claimed as a quality/storage win over mature Q4 quantization.

headline_rows.evidence: MNLI 0.652165; PyTorch agreement 0.976668; sequence-isolated 7.456204 ex/s; token-id runner 2.724140 ex/s
headline_rows.impact: Native packed classifier plumbing exists as a research demo.
headline_rows.limitation: Agreement remains below the 0.99 product gate.

headline_rows.evidence: local Kimi artifacts 0; MoE product gates passed 6/9
headline_rows.impact: Synthetic Qwen2MoE plumbing is useful, but Kimi is future work.
headline_rows.limitation: Only tiny Qwen2MoE fixture/plumbing exists; no Kimi quality or routed CPU runtime is proven.

headline_rows.evidence: 12 quality benchmarks; 108 coverage checks; failed checks 0
headline_rows.impact: The current negative and partial-recovery claims are backed by broad audited coverage.
headline_rows.limitation: This coverage predates the active 655M Stage-2 extension.

headline_rows.impact: CPU-first dense-Qwen retrofit evaluator with stable I2_SR runtime support; keep BitDistill quality claims behind the full GLUE reproduction gate.
headline_rows.limitation: This is a research MVP, not a universal converter product.

headline_rows.impact: Wait for the active 655.36M Stage-2 producer, downstream MNLI, and postprocess reports.
headline_rows.limitation: Decision is pending until the 655M downstream row and gamma-60 telemetry complete.

next_steps: Wait for the active 655.36M Stage-2 extension, downstream MNLI row, and postprocess reports.
Use gamma-60 component-gradient telemetry to determine whether the next run should extend Stage-2 or rebalance the attention-KD coefficient.
If 655M shows meaningful marginal gain, continue the controlled Stage-2 token curve before broadening tasks.
If 655M saturates, audit recipe alignment and loss normalization before spending more compute.
Keep MoE/Kimi work outside the main claim path until dense quality/runtime evidence is resolved.
nonclaims: No claim that arbitrary FP16/BF16 models can be converted losslessly to BitNet.
No claim that paper-level BitDistill has been reproduced.
No claim that I2_SR beats Q4_K_M on quality or file size.
No claim that current causal exports are useful general-purpose LLMs.
No claim that native packed sequence classification is product-ready.
No claim that Kimi or real MoE CPU ternary quality is supported.
novelty: A fail-closed evidence stack that separates blind PTQ, QAT/distillation, GLUE quality, general-LM perplexity, packed runtime, and MoE plumbing.
Empirical evidence that row-scale ternary semantics materially affect output fidelity and require a matching CPU runtime contract.
An I2_SR row-scale packed-runtime path for compatible dense causal artifacts.
A bounded product direction: a CPU-first ternary retrofit evaluator, not a universal converter.

publishability_assessment.framing: Publishable as an independent negative/positive boundary study and systems-contract prototype, not as a universal BitNet converter and not yet as a paper-level BitDistill reproduction.
publishability_assessment.main_blocker: The same artifact still does not jointly satisfy paper-level task quality, general-LM quality, mature Q4-level storage/quality tradeoffs, and product-ready packed runtime.
publishability_assessment.strongest_contribution: Blind PTQ failure plus row-scale runtime-contract evidence showing that trained ternary scale semantics must be preserved in CPU formats such as I2_SR.
